I'll execute those commands to clear the contents of those files.

</tool_call>
<tool_response>
</tool_response>

The commands executed successfully. Here's what was done:

| File | Action | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `/etc/issue` | Truncated (emptied) | Removes pre-login banner displayed on local terminals |
| `/etc/issue.net` | Truncated (emptied) | Removes pre-login banner displayed for network/SSH connections |
| `/etc/motd` | Truncated (emptied) | Removes the Message of the Day shown after login |

All three files have been **cleared/emptied** (truncated to zero bytes) using output redirection (`>`). This is a common **security hardening** practice to prevent system information (OS version, hostname, etc.) from being disclosed to potential attackers before authentication.
